title: Reconfigurable Stream Network Architecture
problem: FPGA-based DNN overlay accelerators suffer from layer-granularity serialization: von Neumann-style coarse-grained ISAs treat each layer instruction atomically, preventing dynamic layer fusion, inter-layer pipelining, and fine-grained bandwidth orchestration across heterogeneous resources (FPGA fabric + AI Engines).
motivation: AI hardware increasingly combines heterogeneous components (e.g., AMD Versal with FPGA fabric + hardened AI Engines), but no existing ISA abstraction unifies resource orchestration and execution-phase transitions at sub-layer granularity, leaving compute units idle during pipeline drains and phase switches.
method: RSN (Reconfigurable Stream Network) abstracts the datapath as a circuit-switched network of stateful functional units (FUs) connected by latency-insensitive data streams. Programming a computation means triggering a path through the FU network; multiple non-conflicting paths enable spatial and pipeline parallelism. A three-level instruction decoder fuses multiple FU uOP streams into a single RSN instruction stream with packet-level reuse to minimize instruction overhead (1 byte drives up to 1.6 GFLOPs). RSN-XNN, the prototype on Versal VCK190, virtualizes both FPGA BRAMs/DSPs and AI Engine tiles as heterogeneous FUs through a common stream interface, enabling dynamic sequential layer pipelining and fine-grained DDR/LPDDR bandwidth interleaving during phase transitions.
key_novelty: RSN introduces a circuit-switched streaming network ISA abstraction that enables dynamic multi-layer pipelining and fine-grained bandwidth orchestration on FPGA overlays without per-layer bitstream reconfiguration—the first FPGA design to achieve this.
contributions: Reconfigurable Stream Network (RSN) ISA abstraction with stateful FU network and latency-insensitive streams
First FPGA overlay enabling dynamic sequential linear-layer pipelining and fine-grained off-chip bandwidth mapping
RSN-XNN prototype on VCK190: 6.1x latency reduction and 2.4x–3.2x throughput improvement over SOTA on same platform
2.1x higher energy efficiency vs. A100 GPU at same 7nm process in FP32; latency parity with T4 GPU at 18% of its memory bandwidth

metrics.speedup: 6.1x latency reduction for BERT vs. SOTA on VCK190; 2.4x–3.2x throughput for BERT/ViT/NCF/MLP
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 2.1x higher energy efficiency in FP32 vs. A100 at same 7nm node
metrics.other: Matches T4 GPU latency with only 18% of its memory bandwidth

baselines: SOTA FPGA DNN overlay on VCK190
limitations: The proof-of-concept RSN-XNN lacks tile-level interleaving (an intentional omission to save circuits), which may limit performance for workloads requiring fine-grained tile-level data reuse.
primary_theme: Circuit-switched streaming ISA for heterogeneous FPGA DNN overlays
